thread:
Incident Bot: ALERT · SLA breach detected for tenant 'aurelia-corp' — 5m P95 latency > 900ms and 4 token-generation errors in last 5m. Paging primary on-call.
Alex G: on it. paging details?
Incident Bot: Page triggered by check `tenant.sla.response_latency.p95` on prod-west-1. Alert threshold = 900ms, window = 5m.
Maria K: I can see a spike in tail latency from embeddings task workers for that tenant starting ~1798504200. Lots of small concurrent jobs from their ingestion pipeline.
Samir P: confirming: most requests that hit >900ms are embedding-create calls. Likely long-running CPU fallback after quantization path fell back to fp16 on some hosts.
Jen L: any error traces?
Maria K: paste logs: ```
2026-02-12T14:18:24Z aurelia-embed-req id=abc123 host=gpu-23 latency_ms=1240 fallback=cpu path=/v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-1
2026-02-12T14:18:26Z aurelia-embed-req id=abc125 host=gpu-09 latency_ms=980 fallback=cpu path=/v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-1
2026-02-12T14:18:27Z aurelia-embed-req id=abc127 host=gpu-23 latency_ms=1450 fallback=cpu path=/v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-1
```
Alex G: hmm gpu-23 and gpu-09 showing fallback=cpu. Could be kernel OOM/driver restart or the quantized kernel not loaded. Samir can you check node health and kernel logs?
Samir P: running `kubectl logs` now. Also checking telemetry for recent container restarts.
SRE Bot: Note: recent kernel-upgrade daemonset rolled to prod-west-1 ~30m ago (job id: ds-20260212-03). Could be related.
Jen L: If kernel upgrade is correlated, this might cause transient failures in optimized kernels -> CPU fallback -> tail latency. Need quick mitigation for customer impact.
Alex G: mitigation options: 1) Temporarily raise the alert threshold for this tenant to 1500ms so we don't keep paging while we remediate; 2) Add 'aurelia-corp' to a watchlist and route pages to a pagingless channel; 3) Apply a per-tenant rate limit to ingestion for a short window; 4) Roll back ds-20260212-03 on affected nodes. Thoughts?
Maria K: I'd prefer #2 + #3 immediately. Raising alert threshold masks true impact for other tenants. But we should avoid noisy pages.
Samir P: I can add the tenant to the quiet watchlist and create a runbook note with `quiet=true` tag so on-call doesn't get paged. I can also throttle concurrent ingestion workers via the tenant throttler (temp limit 20cps).
Alex G: go ahead Samir. Maria keep digging on kernel logs. If we see consistent kernel failures, plan rollback.
Samir P: done — added aurelia-corp to watchlist `quiet-incidents` and created override: `alerts.suppression.aurelia-corp=5m; reason=ongoing mitigation`. Also applied throttling: `tenant.rate_limit.aurelia-corp=20/s` at 1798504600.
Jen L: Thanks. Can we add a dashboard tile for this tenant's embedding latency and fallbacks? Need to see if the throttle actually reduces p95.
Maria K: I created a short-lived dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/aurelia-embed-dash (live) - tile shows p50/p95/p99 and number of fallback=cpu events.
Alex G: monitoring. If p95 drops under 900ms and fallback events stop, we can remove suppression.
SRE Bot: Action logged: incident-1798504322 created, assigned to Alex G / Maria K, mitigation steps saved.
Maria K: initial analysis: 72% of >900ms traces had `fallback=cpu`, and 2 of the affected hosts had `kernel_module:quant_k` crashlooped after the daemonset rollout. I see matching segfaults in dmesg on gpu-23.
Samir P: rolling back ds-20260212-03 on affected nodes now (gpu-23, gpu-09). ETA ~8m.
Alex G: status?
Samir P: rollback complete for the two nodes at 1798505040. Replacing pods and reloading kernels.
Maria K: early signal — fallback events falling. p95 at 14:24 down to 760ms.
Jen L: can we drop suppression? I want to keep watchlist but stop suppressing pages so we still get notified if it resurfaces.
Alex G: agree. Lifting suppression but keep tenant on watchlist + dashboard. Samir remove suppression and keep rate limit until end of incident.
Samir P: suppression removed at 1798505200. Rate limit remains `20/s` until 1798508800.
Incident Bot: NOTE · Alert state moved to WARNING -> no pages.
Alex G: handoff to Jen at 1798506000. Jen you on-call next — summary: kernel rollout caused quant kernel crash on subset of nodes causing CPU fallback for aurelia-corp embedding jobs -> p95 spike and SLA alert. Mitigations: rollback daemonset, temp rate-limit, add to watchlist, dashboard created. Follow-ups: run threshold sweep for tenant-specific checks, add per-tenant kernel health metric, coordinate with infra for canary rollout policy changes.
Jen L: taking handoff. I'll create a follow-up ticket and schedule a short post-incident sync with infra and eng-runtime.
Maria K: also recommend we run a threshold sweep across top 50 tenants to find noisy checks and consider switching per-tenant threshold strategy from static 900ms to dynamic percentile baselining per-tenant.
Alex G: agree. Add to post-incident: (1) threshold sweep script and results, (2) dashboard templates for tenant-level tails, (3) guardrails for daemonset rollouts in prod-west-1.
Jen L: created ticket RW-INC-2026-179850 (link internal) and scheduled 45m sync tomorrow. I'll assign owners: runtime infra (Samir), infra release (Maria), SRE (Alex).
SRE Bot: Reminder: add this thread to the incident record and mark THEME=alert-noise, TENANT=aurelia-corp, ACTIONS=[rollback,rate-limit,watchlist,dashboard,threshold-sweep].
Alex G: thanks team. Leaving notes for postmortem. If it resurfaces I'll wake you. :thumbsup:
Samir P: copy. I'll keep watch on the dashboard and the throttle logs.
Jen L: handoff complete.
Alex G: off-call.
